prompt:
A real photograph, taken with a good phone camera and looking exactly like a phone photograph, of one woman of seventy-nine at home in her living room at home, in the same dark-red armchair, as in the second reference picture, in a wide picture, the person seen from the knees up and filling most of the picture, everything in sharp focus. Natural colours, soft daylight. The textures of real cotton, skin and hair, with the true depth and the slight lens perspective of a photograph.

The first reference picture shows this person: her face, hair and build stay exactly as in it. She wears the same light-blue quilted dressing gown as in the first reference picture. The second reference picture is a real phone photograph of the place: use it for the room, the light and the photographic look, nothing drawn or painted. Its other people do not appear here.

The picture carries no writing, numbers, print, symbol or logo anywhere.

THE PERSON sits upright in her armchair, seen from the front, the whole armchair in the picture. The arm nearer the bed lies stretched along the armrest of the armchair, its sleeve pushed up to the elbow, the bare forearm in full view; her other hand reaches across and grips that bare forearm halfway between the wrist and the elbow, and she looks down at it for a moment before looking up. Her lap lies free under the smooth dressing gown. To the right of the armchair stand the small wooden side table with its coffee cup and the open kitchen doorway; to the left, the care bed with its flowered cover; in front of the armchair, the bare wooden floorboards. The face shows clear, real pain, the way a patient looks when telling the nurse where it hurts: the eyebrows drawn together, the eyes narrowed, the lips pressed together. The look goes towards someone just beside the camera.
